thread:
emma_support: FYI customer Brightline reporting sudden drop in vectors/sec for /v1/embeddings starting ~02:10 UTC. Tokens/sec looks normal. Impacting prod us-west2, percent drop ~60%. sample req_id: req_0a1b2c - can we triage? :eyes:

alex_sre: On it. Do we have any 401/429 spikes in ingress or auth logs around that window? Also want gpu_queue_depth and batch_wait_time graphs.

emma_support: Pasting a couple quick snippets from the customer's request trace and our ingress logs: 
```
2026-03-14T02:10:23Z req=req_0a1b2c route=brightline-prod endpoint=/v1/embeddings status=200 vectors=0 tokens=512 latency=120ms
2026-03-14T02:11:01Z req=req_0a3d4f upstream_auth=401 token_refresh=yes retries=3 -> downstream 200 vectors=0.14
2026-03-14T02:12:05Z req=req_0b4c6e upstream_auth=200 billing=429 X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 retry=1 vectors=0.12
```
Customer metrics: tokens/sec ~1.2k (stable), vectors/sec fell 0.34 -> 0.13.

mike_runtime: Looks like a retry/backoff churn between auth/billing and the vectorization pipeline. If auth or billing calls are blocking the request handler, batchers can't assemble optimal batches -> lots of tiny batches or starvation. Pasting GPU queue depth snapshot: `gpu_queue_depth` jumped from 6 -> 34 at 02:11 UTC. Also seeing increase in `worker_retries_inflight` and `batch_window_ms` trending up. :warning:

jon_eng: Can we reproduce quickly? Steps I use to stress the pipeline: 
```
# reproduce script (small embeddings to emulate customer)
for i in {1..1000}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood/infer/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"short text"}' &\
  if (( i % 50 == 0 )); then sleep 1; fi
done
```
Watch `vectors/sec` in the live dashboard while running. If auth token endpoint is flapping we'll see retries and a divergence between token/sec and vectors/sec.

emma_support: Ran a quick repro in a staging shard: tokens/sec steady ~900/s, vectors/sec dropped from 400/s -> 150/s after simulated auth 401s. Log from agent where it failed to fetch ephemeral billing token: 
```
[2026-03-14T02:11:04Z] billing-client error: 429 Too Many Requests, retry-after=10
[2026-03-14T02:11:04Z] auth-client error: 502 Bad Gateway (token refresh)
```
Seeing both 429 and transient 5xx from auth in same window.

kai_oncall: Short mitigation: routing change to reduce batching pressure for brightline-prod. Temporarily flipped route to `embed-small-v2` (smaller model, lower batch latency) and added conservative `max_concurrency=60` for that customer. Patch applied: 
```
PATCH /v1/routes/brightline-prod
{"model":"embed-small-v2","max_concurrency":60}
```
Early numbers: vectors/sec recovered to ~240/s (still below baseline) but gpu_queue_depth fell to 8.

alex_sre: Good quick mitigation. Longer term: probable root cause is cascading failures from billing/auth causing request handler retries that occupy worker slots and artificially inflate batch_wait_time. Action items: 1) enforce client-side exponential backoff for auth/billing calls in our SDK, 2) respect X-RateLimit-* headers and fail fast with 429 to caller instead of retrying indefinitely, 3) add an admission control on the batcher so auth failures don't hold batcher slots. I'll open RED-8821 and assign to eng-runtime.

jon_eng: For repro + debugging notes: capture a short trace with `X-Trace-Id` and include headers: `X-Customer=brightline-prod`, `X-Debug=1`. Also check KMS token rotation job schedule — if it overlaps it can cause a spike of auth traffic.

emma_support: Filed incident INC-2026-0314-23 and linked customer ticket. Sent Brightline workaround steps (route flip + retry/backoff on their side) and asked them to keep us posted.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-23 | Priority: P2 | Assignee: alex_sre | Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-8821

alex_sre: Follow-ups: deploy small change to auth-client to cap retries=2 and jittered backoff (10ms -> 1000ms), add metrics for `auth_retry_block_time` and `batcher_slot_hold_time`. We'll monitor tomorrow morning window.

kai_oncall: Will leave route override until auth/billing stabilized and then roll back. I'll post a rollback note here when done. :white_check_mark:

emma_support: Thanks team — marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if Brightline reports further regressions.
